newsitem.title: USA: First Midwest to buy SparBank for $105 million.
newsitem.headline: First Midwest to buy SparBank for $105 million.

text.p: First Midwest Bancorp Inc. said Friday it has agreed to acquire SparBank Inc., another Illinois-based banking company, in a stock deal valued at about $105.6 million.
Under the definitive agreement, First Midwest will offer 21.72 common shares for each SparBank share in a tax-free pooling of interests, resulting in the issuance of 3,230,769 First Midwest shares.
First Midwest's stock fell 75 cents to $32 early on Nasdaq.
SparBank is the holding company of the McHenry State Bank in McHenry, Ill., with $445 million in assets.

First Midwest, based in Itasca, Ill., said it expects to take a pretax charge of about $6.5 million in the quarter in which the transaction closes. The charge will be used to convert systems, eliminate excess capacity, pay professional fees and make a one-time provision to bring McHenry State Bank's loan loss reserves to First Midwest's required levels.
First Midwest said the deal is expected to be neutral to its 1997 earnings and boost income by 2 percent to 3 percent in 1998. It will increase First Midwest's assets to about $3.5 billion.

The deal is expected to close by Sept., 30, subject to regulatory approvals, it said. It has been approved by both the board and shareholders of SparBank and the board of First Midwest. First Midwest shareholder approval is not necessary.
In connection with the agreement, First Midwest rescinded the balance of the 900,000 share stock repurchase programme authorised in November 1996.
